title: consolidate-client-cred-cache-and-retry-profiles-improve-stream-consumer-ergonomics
author: Jordan Patel
release_notes: Unified credential cache across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; consolidated retry profile config and defaults; improved streaming consumer ergonomics and backpressure hints; minor SDK semver bumps (py 1.12.0, ts 2.8.0, go 0.9.4); no breaking API changes for typical call sites.
description: Motivation: multiple SDKs had slightly divergent credential caching semantics and retry defaults which caused flap in long-lived streaming clients and inconsistent behaviour across runtimes. This PR centralizes a lightweight on-disk/in-memory credential cache implementation, harmonizes retry profile names and default windows, and smooths streaming consumer ergonomics so application authors get consistent reconnect/backoff and easier-to-reason-about stream iterators across languages. Summary of changes: 1) new cred cache abstraction (CredCache) added to all SDKs with a tiny adapters layer so platform-specific stores (in-memory, file, credential helper) can be swapped; 2) single source-of-truth retry profiles (fast, balanced, conservative) with explicit token refresh windows and jitter rules; 3) streaming consumer helpers (StreamHandle in TS, StreamIterator in Python, StreamReader in Go) that expose a pause/resume/backpressure hint API instead of ad-hoc generators; 4) minor ergonomics: better typed error variants, clearer reconnect exceptions, and safer default timeouts for handshake; 5) docs and CHANGELOG updates and semver bumps for published packages. Compatibility notes: the public call signatures are preserved for standard non-streaming APIs; streaming consumers will need very small updates if they used internal iterator internals (we provide a short migration guide). Testing & CI: unit suites updated for each SDK, e2e session replay harness used to validate long-run stability (48h soak), and cross-language conformance tests exercised retry windows and restart behaviour. Deploy plan: staged release of SDK packages followed by a runtime compatibility gate; rollout pinned to 2 Canary customers for Dedicated before broad rollout. TL;DR: fewer token race cases, consistent retry behaviour, and smoother streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go SDKs.

review_comments: Elena Park: Please ensure the retry window values are documented and provide reasoning for the 75% refresh threshold instead of our previous 60% -- this is subtle and impacts token churn.
Author (Jordan Patel): Answered - moved threshold to 70% after tests showed lower refresh rate reduced hotspotting; added comment and docs section with benchmark data.
Marcus Li: Nit: TS StreamHandle pause() needs a JSDoc example showing recommended usage pattern to avoid lost events during reconnect.
Author: Added example and a small utility (drainWithBackpressure) exposed from the helper module.
Priya Nair: CI flake observed on go integration test when run under race detector; can we add a retry decorator to the sensitive test or fix underlying timing?
Author: Root cause was a tight loop in the test; relaxed timing and added a deterministic hook for CI race builds; reran, green.
ci_summary: All checks passed on final run: unit tests (python/ts/go) green, linters fixed, integration matrix green, e2e soak completed. Two earlier pipeline runs flagged a flaky TS stream test and a go race test; both addressed in follow-up commits and verified.
notes_for_release: Ship SDKs in the following order: typescript@2.8.0, python@1.12.0, go@0.9.4. Recommend coordinating with runtime team to enable compatibility gate and run warmup traffic for 48h. Add migration link to release announcement.
